title: Time I: while, during & every
summary: Expressions for time spans and repetition: {うちに}, {間[あいだ]} / {間[あいだ]に}, {最中[さいちゅう]に}, {たびに}, {ついでに}, {おきに} / {ごとに}, and {から〜にかけて}.

points.title: 〜うちに
points.meaning: while (still) ~ ; before (a state) changes ; (ないうちに) before ~ happens ; in the course of ~
points.structure: Verb (dictionary / ている / ない-form) + うちに ; い-adj + うちに ; な-adj + な + うちに ; Noun + の + うちに
points.explanation:
{〜うちに} has two main uses.

**1. Do it while you can.** The first part describes a state that won't last, and the second part is something you should do before it ends: {熱[あつ]いうちに食[た]べてください。} 'Eat it while it's hot.' {若[わか]いうちに} 'while you're young'. With the {ない}-form, it means 'before something (unwanted) happens': {雨[あめ]が降[ふ]らないうちに帰[かえ]ろう。} 'Let's go home before it rains.'

**2. While doing ~, something changed (without you noticing).** {本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいるうちに、寝[ね]てしまった。} 'While I was reading, I fell asleep.' The first part is usually a continuing action ({〜ている}), and the second part is a change ({〜ようになった}, {〜てしまった}, {だんだん〜}).

The key feeling of {うちに} is 'before the situation changes' or 'the situation changed along the way'.

examples.jp: 熱[あつ]いうちに食[た]べてください。
examples.en: Please eat it while it's hot.

examples.jp: 若[わか]いうちに、いろいろな国[くに]へ行[い]ってみたい。
examples.en: I want to visit lots of countries while I'm young.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]らないうちに、帰[かえ]りましょう。
examples.en: Let's go home before it starts raining.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に住[す]んでいるうちに、納豆[なっとう]が好[す]きになった。
examples.en: Living in Japan, I came to like natto.

examples.jp: 本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいるうちに、寝[ね]てしまった。
examples.en: I fell asleep while I was reading.

quiz.q: 忘[わす]れない＿＿、メモしておこう。
quiz.en: I'll make a note before I forget.

quiz.q: 日本[にほん]のドラマを見[み]ている＿＿、だんだん聞[き]き取[と]れるようになった。
quiz.en: As I kept watching Japanese dramas, I gradually became able to catch what they were saying.

points.title: 〜間[あいだ] / 〜間[あいだ]に
points.meaning: (間) for the whole time that ~ ; (間に) at some point during ~
points.structure: Verb (ている) + 間[あいだ] / 間[あいだ]に ; Noun + の + 間[あいだ] / 間[あいだ]に
points.explanation:
{間[あいだ]} means 'interval' or 'space between'. The particle {に} makes a big difference.

- **{〜間[あいだ]} (no {に}):** something continues for the **whole** period. The second part is a continuing action or state: {夏休[なつやす]みの間[あいだ]、ずっと実家[じっか]にいました。} 'I was at my parents' place the whole summer vacation.'
- **{〜間[あいだ]に}:** something happens **at one point within** the period. The second part is a one-time event: {夏休[なつやす]みの間[あいだ]に、運転免許[うんてんめんきょ]を取[と]りたい。} 'I want to get my driver's license during the summer vacation.'

**{間[あいだ]に} vs {うちに}:** {間[あいだ]に} is a neutral time span with a clear beginning and end. {うちに} adds the feeling of 'before it changes / while I still can', and is the natural choice with states like {若[わか]い} and {熱[あつ]い}. When there's a clear period like 'while the kids are asleep', both are often possible.

examples.jp: 夏休[なつやす]みの間[あいだ]、ずっと実家[じっか]にいました。
examples.en: I was at my parents' home for the whole summer vacation.

examples.jp: 夏休[なつやす]みの間[あいだ]に、運転免許[うんてんめんきょ]を取[と]りたい。
examples.en: I want to get my driver's license during summer vacation.

examples.jp: 私[わたし]が電話[でんわ]している間[あいだ]、子供[こども]たちは静[しず]かに待[ま]っていた。
examples.en: The children waited quietly the whole time I was on the phone.

examples.jp: 留守[るす]の間[あいだ]に、荷物[にもつ]が届[とど]いていた。
examples.en: A package arrived while I was out.

examples.jp: 部長[ぶちょう]が出張[しゅっちょう]している間[あいだ]に、この資料[しりょう]を準備[じゅんび]しておきましょう。
examples.en: Let's get these materials ready while the manager is away on his business trip.

quiz.q: 会議[かいぎ]の＿＿、ずっと携帯[けいたい]の電源[でんげん]を切[き]っていた。
quiz.en: I kept my phone switched off for the whole meeting.

quiz.q: 私[わたし]がシャワーを浴[あ]びている＿＿、友達[ともだち]から電話[でんわ]があった。
quiz.en: While I was taking a shower, a friend called.

points.title: 〜最中[さいちゅう]に
points.meaning: right in the middle of ~ (when something happens / interrupts)
points.structure: Verb (ている) + 最中[さいちゅう]に ; Noun + の + 最中[さいちゅう]に ; 〜最中[さいちゅう]だ
points.explanation:
{〜最中[さいちゅう]に} means 'right in the middle of ~', at the very peak of an activity. The second part is usually something **unexpected** that interrupts it, often something annoying.

{会議[かいぎ]の最中[さいちゅう]に、電話[でんわ]が鳴[な]った。} 'Right in the middle of the meeting, a phone rang.'

You can also end a sentence with {最中[さいちゅう]だ} to say you're busy in the middle of something: {今[いま]考[かんが]えている最中[さいちゅう]だから、ちょっと待[ま]って。} 'I'm in the middle of thinking, so hang on.'

Compared with {間[あいだ]に}, {最中[さいちゅう]に} focuses on the busiest, most active moment and the surprise of the interruption. It's used with activities, not with states like {若[わか]い}.

examples.jp: 会議[かいぎ]の最中[さいちゅう]に、電話[でんわ]が鳴[な]った。
examples.en: Right in the middle of the meeting, a phone rang.

examples.jp: 料理[りょうり]をしている最中[さいちゅう]に、停電[ていでん]した。
examples.en: The power went out right in the middle of my cooking.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]の最中[さいちゅう]に、お腹[なか]が痛[いた]くなった。
examples.en: In the middle of the exam, I got a stomachache.

examples.jp: 今[いま]、考[かんが]えている最中[さいちゅう]だから、ちょっと待[ま]って。
examples.en: I'm right in the middle of thinking, so wait a moment.

quiz.q: 今[いま]、資料[しりょう]を作[つく]っている＿＿だから、少[すこ]し待[ま]ってください。
quiz.en: I'm in the middle of making the materials right now, so please wait a little.

quiz.q: 食事[しょくじ]の＿＿に地震[じしん]が起[お]きて、びっくりした。
quiz.en: An earthquake hit right in the middle of our meal, and I was startled.

points.title: 〜たびに
points.structure: Verb (dictionary) + たびに ; Noun + の + たびに
points.explanation:
{〜たびに} means 'every time A happens, B happens too'. {たび} means 'occasion', so it's literally 'on every occasion of A'.

{この歌[うた]を聞[き]くたびに、学生時代[がくせいじだい]を思[おも]い出[だ]す。} 'Every time I hear this song, I remember my student days.'

It works with verbs in the dictionary form and with nouns that describe events: {出張[しゅっちょう]のたびに} 'every business trip', {引[ひ]っ越[こ]しのたびに} 'every time I move'.

It is close to {〜とき（は）いつも}, but {たびに} emphasizes that B reliably follows A each time, often with a sense of repetition or gradual change.

examples.jp: この歌[うた]を聞[き]くたびに、学生時代[がくせいじだい]を思[おも]い出[だ]す。
examples.en: Every time I hear this song, I remember my student days.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは出張[しゅっちょう]のたびに、お土産[みやげ]を買[か]ってきてくれる。
examples.en: Every time Tanaka goes on a business trip, he brings us back a souvenir.

examples.jp: 祖母[そぼ]は、会[あ]うたびに「大[おお]きくなったね」と言[い]う。
examples.en: Every time I see my grandmother, she says, 'You've grown!'

examples.jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しのたびに、物[もの]が少[すこ]しずつ減[へ]っていく。
examples.en: Each time I move, I have a few less things.

quiz.q: 実家[じっか]に帰[かえ]る＿＿、母[はは]がたくさん料理[りょうり]を作[つく]ってくれる。
quiz.en: Every time I go back to my parents' home, my mother cooks lots of food for me.

quiz.q: あの写真[しゃしん]を見[み]る＿＿、楽[たの]しかった旅行[りょこう]を思[おも]い出[だ]します。
quiz.en: Every time I look at that photo, I remember that fun trip.

points.title: 〜ついでに
points.meaning: while (you're) at it ; taking the opportunity of ~ (to also do something extra)
points.structure: Verb (dictionary / た-form) + ついでに ; Noun + の + ついでに
points.explanation:
{〜ついでに} means you're already doing A, so you **take the opportunity** to do B as well. A is the main purpose; B is a small extra that's convenient to do at the same time.

{コンビニに行[い]くついでに、この手紙[てがみ]を出[だ]してくれない？} 'Since you're going to the convenience store anyway, could you post this letter for me?'

The same person does both A and B. Nouns that describe activities take {の}: {散歩[さんぽ]のついでに} 'while out on a walk', {買[か]い物[もの]のついでに} 'while out shopping'.

On its own, {ついでに} can also start a sentence: {ついでに、これもお願[ねが]いできますか。} 'While you're at it, could you do this too?'

examples.jp: コンビニに行[い]くついでに、この手紙[てがみ]を出[だ]してくれない？
examples.en: Since you're going to the convenience store, could you post this letter for me?

examples.jp: 散歩[さんぽ]のついでに、パンを買[か]ってきた。
examples.en: I picked up some bread while I was out for a walk.

examples.jp: 東京[とうきょう]へ出張[しゅっちょう]したついでに、昔[むかし]の友達[ともだち]に会[あ]った。
examples.en: While I was in Tokyo on business, I took the chance to see an old friend.

examples.jp: 部屋[へや]を掃除[そうじ]するついでに、いらない服[ふく]も捨[す]てた。
examples.en: While cleaning my room, I also threw out clothes I didn't need.

quiz.q: 郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]へ行[い]った＿＿、銀行[ぎんこう]にも寄[よ]った。
quiz.en: While I was at the post office, I stopped by the bank too.

quiz.q: 買[か]い物[もの]の＿＿、駅前[えきまえ]の本屋[ほんや]をのぞいてみた。
quiz.en: While I was out shopping, I took a look in the bookstore in front of the station.

points.title: 〜おきに / 〜ごとに
points.meaning: (おきに) at intervals of ~ ; every other ~ ; (ごとに) every ~ ; each ~
points.structure: Number + counter + おきに ; Number + counter + ごとに ; Noun + ごとに ; Verb (dictionary) + ごとに
points.explanation:
Both express regular repetition, but they count differently.

**{ごとに}** = 'every / each': {一日[いちにち]ごとに} = every day. {二時間[にじかん]ごとに} = every two hours. It also attaches to nouns: {季節[きせつ]ごとに} 'each season', {チームごとに} 'each team'.

**{おきに}** = 'with ~ in between': {一日[いちにち]おきに} = every **other** day (Monday, Wednesday, Friday…), because one day is skipped between.

For continuous quantities like minutes or meters, the two mean almost the same thing: {十五分[じゅうごふん]おきに} and {十五分[じゅうごふん]ごとに} are both 'every 15 minutes'. The difference only matters with units like days, floors, or stops.

examples.jp: このバスは十五分[じゅうごふん]おきに来[き]ます。
examples.en: This bus comes every fifteen minutes.

examples.jp: 一日[いちにち]おきにジムに通[かよ]っている。
examples.en: I go to the gym every other day.

examples.jp: 二時間[にじかん]ごとに休憩[きゅうけい]を取[と]ってください。
examples.en: Please take a break every two hours.

examples.jp: この町[まち]では、季節[きせつ]ごとに違[ちが]う景色[けしき]が楽[たの]しめる。
examples.en: In this town you can enjoy different scenery each season.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]に着[つ]くごとに、乗客[じょうきゃく]が増[ふ]えていった。
examples.en: With each station we stopped at, there were more passengers.

quiz.q: 月曜[げつよう]、水曜[すいよう]、金曜[きんよう]と、一日[いちにち]＿＿日本語[にほんご]のレッスンがある。
quiz.en: I have Japanese lessons every other day: Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

quiz.q: 会議[かいぎ]では、チーム＿＿意見[いけん]を発表[はっぴょう]することになった。
quiz.en: It was decided that each team will present its opinion at the meeting.

points.title: 〜から〜にかけて
points.meaning: from ~ through ~ ; over the period / area from ~ to ~ (a rough span)
points.structure: Noun + から + Noun + にかけて
points.explanation:
{AからBにかけて} describes a span of time or space from A to B, without exact edges. It's the standard phrase in weather forecasts.

{今夜[こんや]から明日[あした]の朝[あさ]にかけて、雨[あめ]が強[つよ]く降[ふ]るでしょう。} 'Heavy rain is expected from tonight through tomorrow morning.'

**{にかけて} vs {まで}:** {AからBまで} gives exact start and end points: {九時[くじ]から五時[ごじ]まで働[はたら]く} 'I work from 9 to 5.' {AからBにかけて} gives a fuzzy range — something is happening somewhere across that span, possibly not all of it. So don't use {にかけて} for precise schedules.

It also works on its own after one noun: {週末[しゅうまつ]にかけて} 'heading into the weekend'.

examples.jp: 今夜[こんや]から明日[あした]の朝[あさ]にかけて、雨[あめ]が強[つよ]く降[ふ]るでしょう。
examples.en: Heavy rain is expected from tonight through tomorrow morning.

examples.jp: 関東[かんとう]から東北[とうほく]にかけて、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]っています。
examples.en: Snow is falling across the region from Kanto to Tohoku.

examples.jp: 毎年[まいとし]三月[さんがつ]から四月[しがつ]にかけて、桜[さくら]が咲[さ]きます。
examples.en: Every year the cherry blossoms bloom from March into April.

examples.jp: 年末[ねんまつ]から年始[ねんし]にかけて、多[おお]くの会社[かいしゃ]が休[やす]みになる。
examples.en: Many companies close over the New Year period.

quiz.q: 九州[きゅうしゅう]から四国[しこく]＿＿、大雨[おおあめ]に注意[ちゅうい]してください。
quiz.en: Please watch out for heavy rain across the area from Kyushu to Shikoku.

quiz.q: 来週[らいしゅう]の月曜日[げつようび]＿＿水曜日[すいようび]にかけて、出張[しゅっちょう]で大阪[おおさか]にいます。
quiz.en: From next Monday through Wednesday, I'll be in Osaka on a business trip.
